I am an agronomist and member of the Ordre des agronomes du Québec with 15 years of experience in agricultural data analysis. My work sits at the intersection of field agronomy and quantitative analysis — two ways of reading the same landscape.

**Background**

I started my career in swine production at Génétiporc, where I managed performance monitoring across farrowing, nursery, and finishing stages: data collection, gap identification, and genetic project coordination. At Logiag, as the agronomist responsible for a swine integrator, I added a regulatory and field dimension — PAEF development, phosphorus balances, farm visits, and soil sampling. I later shifted toward large-scale data analysis, including modelling soil organic carbon in agricultural fields.

I hold a M.Sc. in Animal Science from University Laval focused on reducing phosphorus excretion in rainbow trout, and I have recently worked as a research professional modelling phosphorus dynamics in freshwater aquaculture systems.

**Today**

I work independently on agri-environmental data analysis mandates and I am developing GeoAgro — a geospatial diagnostic tool for agricultural land, combining agronomic and environmental data.

This site is a space to share my approach to agronomy: rigorous, data-grounded, and always oriented toward concrete decisions in the field.

For professional inquiries: [contact form](https://tally.so/r/gDZMrJ)
